subject: Estimating Thetas (Person Parameters) from Known Items

messages.author: b5ebbeae393deb7d
messages.subject: Estimating Thetas (Person Parameters) from Known Items
parts:
Hi all,

I expect this is a very basic question, for which I apologize.  But my google-fu has failed to provide an answer to this question for me.

I have a set of 5 items that have been calibrated (by someone else) in a unidimensional partial credit model on many thousands of people.  So the thresholds are "known".   I have a new set of participants for whom I wish to estimate the theta values.  I tried to do this with mirt() using the following model specification:

spec2 <- 'F = 1-5
         START = (1-5, a1, 1.0),(1,b1,-2.67352),(1,b2,-0.75848),(1,b3,1.4466),(2,b1,-1.75534),(2,b2,0.75861),(2,b3,2.14270),(3,b1,-1.88493),(3,b2,0.77738),(3,b3,2.36029),(4,b1,-1.65128),(4,b2,0.97329),(4,b3,2.34365),(5,b1,-2.11797),(5,b2,-0.92395),(5,b3,0.96295)
         FIXED = (1-5, a1),(1-5,b1),(1-5,b2),(1-5,b3)
         FREE = (GROUP, COV_11)'

The START stuff is all one one line in my R code.

This, however failed to work, and I can't discover the correct way to accomplish my goal.  Everything I can find (including in this group) seems to assume that you are trying to find the item characteristics rather than the person characteristics.  Any help would be appreciated.

regards

Jamie

parts:
This is just an observation.  The traditional2mirt function did not provide usable values (at least as I interpreted them).  For the input slope & thresholds of 

a=1, b1= -2.67352, b2=-0.75848 , b3= 1.44660

traditional2mirt returned values of 

     a1     ak0     ak1     ak2     ak3      d0      d1      d2      d3 
1.00000 0.00000 1.00000 2.00000 3.00000 0.00000 2.67352 3.43200 1.98540

which mirt() balked at because the d1, d2, d3 are not in descending order.  (I didn't specify the ak values in the parameter file, which could be the problem?)

I used the alternate formula provided by Felix (and also this post - https://groups.google.com/g/mirt-package/c/YvM53xXlQaE ) d = -b (because a=1 - I'm running pcm not gpcm) and that allowed mirt() to run and correctly reproduced the a and b values in the output. 

Thanks, Felix for setting me on the right path.

Jamie

Okay - thank you for that.  I'll take a look at the traditional2mirt function and hopefully get it working.

regards

Jamie

parts:
hi,

the ak0, ak1, ... look like from a gpcm, whereas the d=-b/a is for the grm, i think. traditional2mirt has a cls argument where you can specify the model. to get the most suitable parameter table, you can do something like

mirt(data, 1, itemtype = "gpcm", pars = "values")

and then adapt the values.

best, felix
